full_text:
P L D 1999 Lahore 33

Before Malik MuOmmad Qayyum, J

MUHAMMAD AI~RAM‐‐‐Petitioner

versus

Mst. RAHEELA ASLAM .4nd 2 others‐‐‐Respondents

Writ Petition No. 19031 of 1998, decided on 17th September, 1998.

West Pakistan Family Courts Act (XXXV of 1964)‐‐‐

‐‐‐‐S. 14‐‐‐Appeal against interlocutory order‐‐‐Maintainability‐‐‐Pending suit defence of defendant was struck off and case was adjourned for evidence of plaintiff‐‐‐Order striking off defence was challenged by defendant by filing appeal which was dismissed by Additional District Judge on ground that appeal against interlocutory order did not lie‐‐Defendant had contended that under S.14 of West Pakistan Family Courts Act, 1964 not only a decree, but also any decision of Family Court was appealable and that even if order was interlocutory in nature, that amounted to decision and could be appealed against‐‐‐Contention of defendant was repelled because although S.14 of West Pakistan Family Courts Act, 1964 mentioned word "decision" but that had to be read ejusdem generis and must take colour from use of word "decree" ‐‐‐Only final orders would be covered by word "decision"‐‐‐Appeal against interlocutory order, thus, was rightly held to be incompetent.

S. Azharul Hassan Naqvi v. Mst. Hamida Bibi and 2 others 1979 CLC 754 ref.

Malik Abdul Majeed Chaudhry for Petitioner

ORDER

The dispute in this petition arises out of a pending suit under the West Pakistan Family Courts Act, 1964 filed by respondent No. l against the petitioner in which his defence was struck off on 30‐3‐1998 and the case was adjourned for evidence of respondent No. 1. This order was challenged by the petitioner by filing an appeal which was dismissed by the Additional District Judge on 31‐7‐1998 on the ground that the appeal against the interlocutory order does not lie.

2. The learned counsel for the petitioner has contended that under section 14 of the West Pakistan Family Courts Act, 1964 not only a decree but I also any decision of the Family Court is appealable and even if the order is interlocutory in nature, it amounts to decision and could be appealed against. This contention of the learned counsel for the petitioner is without any force.

3. Although it is true that section 14 mentions the word "decision" but it has been held by various Courts that this has to be read ejusdem generis and A must take colour from the use of the word "decree" in the said section and only final orders would be covered by the word "decision". If any authority is needed, reference may be made to S. Azharul Hassan Naqvi v. Mst. Hamida Bibi and 2 others 1979 CLC 754. In this view of the matter, the learned Additional District Judge was correct in holding that the appeal before him was not competent.

4. Be that as it may, the petitioner is not remedyless inasmuch as if a decree is ultimately passed against him by the Family Court, he can file an appeal against the decision or the decree wherein he may challenge interim order, if he so desires.

Disposed of in the above terms

H.B.T./M‐825/L Order accordingly

final_orders.sentence: Disposed of in the above terms
final_orders.label: disposed_accordingly
